## Cantor–Bendixson derivatives

Let $X$ be a topological space and $I(X)$ the set of its isolated points. The derivatives of $X$ are defined by recursion:
$$
X^{(0)} = X, \qquad
X^{(\xi+1)} = X^{(\xi)} \setminus I\bigl(X^{(\xi)}\bigr), \qquad
X^{(\lambda)} = \bigcap_{\xi<\lambda} X^{(\xi)} \text{ for limit $\lambda$.}
$$ {#eq-derivatives}

::: {#lem-closed}
For every ordinal $\xi$, the derivative $X^{(\xi)}$ is closed in $X$.
:::

::: {.proof}
By induction on $\xi$, using ([-@eq-derivatives]): $I(X^{(\xi)})$ is open in $X^{(\xi)}$, and intersections of closed sets are closed.
:::

::: {#thm-juhasz-weiss}
## Juhász–Weiss
For every ordinal $\alpha < \omega_2$ there is a locally compact, Hausdorff, scattered space $X$ with $\CS(X) = \langle \omega \rangle_\alpha$.
:::

By @lem-closed, each level is open in a closed subspace; @thm-juhasz-weiss is due to @juhasz-weiss1978.
